thesis: Fermi Inc. (Fermi America) is a Texas-based developer building **Project Matador**, a gigawatt-scale private power and powered-shell artificial intelligence campus in Carson County. **[Fact]** The company elects REIT tax status and expects substantially all future revenue from long-term lease rental income paid by hyperscale tenants once data-center shells are delivered. **[Fact]** As of March 31, 2026, Fermi had **not** commenced revenue-generating activities; the quarter reflected site development, equipment procurement, and commercial marketing. **[Fact]** The campus is planned for roughly **11 gigawatts** of on-demand generation (expandable toward **17 gigawatts**) and about **15 million square feet** of AI-ready space, using on-site gas, solar, battery storage, and longer-dated nuclear baseload. **[Fact]** The company was formed in January 2025 and listed on Nasdaq in September 2025.
why_market_wrong: The market may treat Fermi either as a failed tenant story after the September 2025 non-binding letter of intent expired, or as a speculative nuclear developer, when the filing picture is closer to a pre-lease infrastructure REIT with **$1.4 billion** of capitalized project assets and permitted gas capacity already on the balance sheet. **[Inference]** Governance noise (CEO termination, proxy contest, securities litigation) can obscure that vertical construction is explicitly gated on a definitive tenant lease, not on speculative science-project timelines. **[Inference]** If hyperscaler power scarcity persists, the predictive attribute is a **dated catalyst**: first powered-shell commercial operations targeted for **2027** once a binding lease triggers vertical build.
